description: Static, curated knowledge base for per-patch algorithm selection (structured filters + BM25, top-1). No LLM. Edit in source control; validated at start-up.

selector.tie_break: higher BM25 score, then lower algorithm id
selector.capacity_source: measured by the algorithm implementation on the patch (KB capacity text is advisory only)

query_terms_note: Thresholds are local heuristics (kind=local_heuristic); they only decide which descriptive terms enter the BM25 query.

evidence_kinds.local_heuristic: maintainer judgement, not a published result; validate with the listed experiment

citation_note: DOIs were entered from the maintainers' reference list and are not machine-verified in this build; check the DOI record before citing.

entries.name: lsb_replacement
entries.summary: Overwrites the least significant bit of consecutive patch samples with payload bits.
suitable_when: noisy or high-entropy patches where LSB planes already look random
small, thin or ragged patches (no geometry requirement)
chunks that need a high bit rate
avoid_when: smooth or flat patches (pairs-of-values artefacts are most visible to steganalysis there)
saturated patches (LSB plane of 0/255 areas is constant in the cover)

capacity.behavior: 1 bit per sample of the patch (3 per RGB pixel)

distortion.impact: at most +/-1 on half of the used samples (expected MSE 0.5 on used samples)

entries.assumptions: 8-bit L or RGB, lossless PNG; all channels used
entries.extraction: read LSBs of the same raster-order patch samples; needs only the patch mask and chunk length
limitations: statistically detectable (chi-square / RS / sample-pair analysis)
destroyed by any lossy processing

evidence.claim: LSB replacement creates pairs-of-values asymmetry that chi-square and RS analysis detect
Preferring noisy/high-entropy patches for this method
evidence.validate: Learning workbench -> patch survey: compare PSNR/SSIM and extraction on patches with and without the stated characteristic.

entries.name: lsb_matching
entries.variant: lsb-matching-pm1-seeded-v2 (patch samples; sign stream seeded per patch from the cover hash)
entries.summary: Changes a sample by +1 or -1 only when its LSB differs from the payload bit.
suitable_when: textured or noisy patches
irregular patches of any shape
medium to high bit rates where coding-based methods lack capacity
avoid_when: smooth patches (histogram smoothing is easier to detect)

capacity.behavior: 1 bit per sample of the patch

distortion.impact: +/-1 on about half of the used samples; avoids the pairs-of-values artefact

cost.notes: one seeded random draw per bit

entries.extraction: read LSBs of the same patch samples; the sign stream is not needed
limitations: detectable by histogram-characteristic-function and rich-model steganalysis
destroyed by lossy processing

evidence.claim: +/-1 embedding removes the pairs-of-values asymmetry but remains detectable in grayscale images
Variant: per-patch seeded sign stream (not a secret key)
Preferring textured/noisy patches
evidence.validate: Learning workbench -> patch survey: compare PSNR/SSIM and extraction on patches with and without the stated characteristic.

entries.name: pvd
entries.summary: Hides 3-7 bits in the difference of a sample pair; larger differences carry more bits.
suitable_when: edge-rich or high-contrast patches (large differences carry more bits)
chunks that need the highest capacity
avoid_when: smooth patches at low rate (every used pair is re-quantised, changes can exceed 1 level)

distortion.impact: individual samples can change by several levels, concentrated where differences are large

entries.assumptions: 8-bit L or RGB, lossless PNG; pairs are consecutive entries of the patch sample list
entries.extraction: recompute |a'-b'| per pair; the range of a pair is preserved by embedding, so positions re-synchronise from the stego image
limitations: histogram steps at range boundaries are statistically detectable
destroyed by lossy processing

evidence.claim: Wu-Tsai range table and the edge/smooth capacity argument
Variant: pairs are consecutive patch samples (for RGB this pairs neighbouring channels), not strictly horizontal neighbours as in the paper

entries.name: edge_adaptive_lsb
entries.summary: LSB replacement only on pixels whose 7-MSB gradient reaches a threshold (default 6).
suitable_when: patches with clear edges and a small chunk
when changes should stay off flat areas
avoid_when: patches with few edges (little or no capacity)

capacity.behavior: one bit per sample of each eligible (edge) pixel inside the patch; can be zero

cost.notes: gradient of the patch bounding box

entries.assumptions: 8-bit L or RGB, lossless PNG; RGB uses an integer luma of the 7-MSB planes
entries.extraction: rebuild the mask from the stego patch (7 MSBs are never modified by this method), read LSBs
limitations: simplified mask, not the LSBMR scheme of the cited paper
statistically detectable as an LSB-class method

evidence.claim: Edge regions tolerate embedding better than smooth regions; edge-adaptive selection
Variant: threshold on a 7-MSB gradient computed only from pixels inside the patch

entries.name: dct
entries.summary: Quantisation-index modulation of 6 mid-frequency coefficients per complete 8x8 block.
suitable_when: compact, block-aligned patches with moderate texture
low-rate chunks
avoid_when: ragged or thin patches without complete blocks

capacity.behavior: 6 bits per complete 8x8 block of the global grid inside the patch

distortion.impact: coefficients move by up to one quantisation step (12); highest per-block distortion with dct_svd

entries.assumptions: 8-bit; gray plane or the blue plane of RGB; lossless PNG
entries.extraction: same blocks (complete 8x8 blocks inside the mask, raster order), parity of round(X/delta)
limitations: not robust to JPEG in this implementation
refuses blocks that fail verification

evidence.claim: QIM embedding principle
Saturation threshold 0.02 as a hard exclusion
evidence.validate: tests/test_patch_algorithms.py::test_dct_saturated_patch_is_filtered and the workbench patch survey on the B/W cover

entries.name: dwt
entries.summary: One bit per complete 2x2 block in the Haar diagonal detail coefficient.
suitable_when: flat, saturated or two-level (black/white) patches where LSB-style and DCT methods are unsuitable
low-rate chunks
avoid_when: chunks needing more than 0.25 bit per pixel

capacity.behavior: 1 bit per complete 2x2 block of the embedding plane

distortion.impact: HH moves by up to two steps of delta=4, spread over four pixels

cost.notes: vectorised Haar step with per-block verification

entries.assumptions: 8-bit; gray plane or the blue plane of RGB; lossless PNG
limitations: not robust to JPEG/resizing (measured)
one concrete Haar/QIM variant, not a canonical DWT scheme

evidence.claim: QIM principle
Works on saturated black/white covers through alternative pixel patterns
evidence.validate: tests: transform methods on the procedural B/W cover

entries.name: dct_svd
entries.sub_domain: block DCT + SVD, QIM on sigma_1
entries.summary: One bit per complete 8x8 block in the largest singular value of a mid-band DCT sub-matrix.
suitable_when: large, compact, block-aligned patches
very small chunks
avoid_when: small or ragged patches (1 bit per 64 pixels)

capacity.behavior: 1 bit per complete 8x8 block; lowest capacity of the ten

distortion.impact: sigma_1 moves by up to one step (16), spread over 64 pixels

entries.assumptions: 8-bit; gray plane or the blue plane of RGB; lossless PNG
limitations: one concrete member of the DCT-SVD family; the cited paper is a watermarking scheme and differs
not robust to JPEG here

evidence.claim: DCT-SVD family (watermarking)
This variant (region, rule, step) is repository specific

entries.name: hugo
entries.variant: HUGO additive approximation: exact single-change costs (T=90, sigma=1, gamma=1) + binary STC h=7, no model correction
entries.summary: Minimises a weighted change of pixel-difference co-occurrences; embeds with syndrome-trellis codes.
suitable_when: textured, noisy patches with many samples
low-rate chunks (more samples per bit lower the distortion)
avoid_when: chunks above 0.5 bit per sample (no capacity)

capacity.behavior: at most min(samples, 131072)/2 bits; the planner uses up to 10 samples per bit

distortion.impact: +/-1 on few samples, placed where the co-occurrence model changes least

cost.notes: per-sample cost evaluation + Viterbi over 128 states

entries.assumptions: 8-bit L or RGB (each channel treated as a plane), lossless PNG; binary syndrome-trellis codes, constraint height 7, deterministic non-optimised submatrices (not the published tables)
entries.extraction: syndrome of the LSBs of the same permuted patch samples; needs mask, chunk length and w
limitations: additive approximation without model correction, not canonical HUGO
sigma and gamma not re-verified against the full paper text
public permutation (no stego key)

evidence.claim: HUGO distortion (weighted co-occurrence differences, T=90)
STC minimises additive distortion
Single-change additive costs, custom STC submatrices, per-patch domain

entries.name: wow
entries.variant: WOW (p=-1, db8 filter bank) + binary STC h=7
entries.summary: Costs are low only where the content is textured in every direction; embeds with syndrome-trellis codes.
suitable_when: cluttered, high-frequency patches
low-rate chunks

distortion.impact: +/-1 on few samples, avoiding smooth areas and clean edges

cost.notes: three filter passes per channel (once per cover) + Viterbi

entries.assumptions: 8-bit L or RGB (per channel), lossless PNG; binary syndrome-trellis codes, constraint height 7, deterministic non-optimised submatrices (not the published tables)
entries.extraction: syndrome of the LSBs of the same permuted patch samples
limitations: cost map is computed on the whole cover (read-only) and indexed by the patch
public permutation (no stego key)
distortion minimisation is not proof of undetectability

evidence.claim: WOW cost: reciprocal aggregation of directional residual suitabilities
Aggregation aligned with the exact adjoint; custom STC submatrices

entries.name: s_uniward
entries.variant: S-UNIWARD (spatial, sigma=1, db8 filter bank) + binary STC h=7
entries.summary: Cost = relative change of directional wavelet coefficients; embeds with syndrome-trellis codes.
suitable_when: patches mixing smooth and textured content (the cost map steers changes to the textured part)
low-rate chunks
general natural content

distortion.impact: +/-1 on few samples where wavelet coefficients change least in relative terms

cost.notes: three filter passes per channel (once per cover) + Viterbi

entries.assumptions: 8-bit L or RGB (per channel), lossless PNG; binary syndrome-trellis codes, constraint height 7, deterministic non-optimised submatrices (not the published tables)
entries.extraction: syndrome of the LSBs of the same permuted patch samples
limitations: spatial variant only (not J-UNIWARD)
public permutation (no stego key)
distortion minimisation is not proof of undetectability

evidence.claim: UNIWARD distortion and its additive approximation
Per-patch STC domain; custom STC submatrices
